drhp.one_liner: Timken India Limited is the Indian arm of The Timken Company, manufacturing and selling anti-friction bearings and related components for railways, core industrial sectors, commercial vehicles and tractors, serving both OEMs and the aftermarket through direct and indirect sales and service models.

plants.role: New manufacturing plant set up to manufacture Spherical Roller Bearings and Cylindrical Roller Bearings; commercial production started in Q2 2025-26. A manufacturing line for plain bearings (GGB brand, Fiber reinforced composite material) is being set up at this facility.
Manufacturing facilities serving the rail market; capacity of bearing components (cup and cone) at the rail facility is being enhanced.

risks.note: Global activity faces a major test from the outbreak of war in the Middle East, with global growth forecast to decelerate to 3.1 percent in 2026 from 3.4 percent in 2025 and a larger net impact expected on emerging markets; the Chairman also describes an environment marked by geopolitical uncertainties, evolving trade dynamics and changing industrial supply chains
risks.risk: Geopolitical conflict and slowing global growth

risks.note: India meets more than 85 percent of its crude oil requirements through imports with approximately half transiting the Strait of Hormuz, so the conflict poses the risk of a significant terms-of-trade shock that could increase input costs, exert downward pressure on the rupee, and complicate inflation-growth trade-offs

Profit before tax as a percentage of revenue from operations declined compared with the previous year mainly due to increased cost of material consumed, increased depreciation charges and reduction in other income, with net material cost rising modestly faster than revenue growth

Bringing a new site online requires patience and perseverance; as Bharuch ramps up the Company continues to incur initial operating costs and fund capability building, and higher depreciation from the new manufacturing plant added to other expenses
risks.risk: Execution and ramp-up drag from the new Bharuch plant

risks.note: Demand is tied to government capex and industry cycles — Indian Railways budgetary support, steel and cement capacity expansion, thermal PowerGen commissioning, mining output targets and infrastructure-led commercial vehicle demand — so any slowdown in public capex directly affects the bearing demand base
risks.risk: Cyclicality and policy dependence of end markets

risks.note: The record FY 2026 tractor upcycle was partly driven by pre-buying ahead of TREM V norms effective April 2026, which can borrow volumes from the following year even as the CV cycle is expected to moderate to efficiency-driven growth in FY 27
risks.risk: Pull-forward of tractor demand ahead of TREM V norms

risks.note: The Company runs material arm's length transactions with group entities — The Timken Company (Ultimate Holding Company, including royalty), The Timken Corporation and Timken Wuxi Bearings Co. Ltd. (fellow subsidiaries) — for purchases and sales of goods, making sourcing, offtake and technology access dependent on the parent group and requiring recurring Board and shareholder approvals

Revenue growth for the year was primarily driven by strong export sales with volume growth across geographical locations while domestic revenue showed modest growth, leaving the Company exposed to higher trade barriers and reconfiguration of trade flows and supply chains
